result:
Round 288 is implemented and ready for C. The report is in `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-288.md`, with scripts and screenshots in `a-round-288/`. The claims check matched `claims-288-output.txt` before I edited anything.

**Changes (only the granted lines; `git status` still shows exactly the 7 paths from round 287):**
- **`store.tsx` and `ProductCard.tsx`:** the "Price unavailable" label now carries `leading-8` and `leading-7`, so it keeps the same 32 px and 28 px line height as a known price. The known-price lines are byte-identical.
- **`product-utils.ts`:** an invalid synthetic Premium price (−5, Infinity) becomes "unknown" and reads "Price unavailable", the same as the purchase panel. The check that decides whether a Premium version exists is unchanged, so 0 and NaN still add no Premium.
- **Tests:** the three class checks in §3.1 were replaced, not removed. PR10 and VC5 were added. PR10 has one extra NaN check that the reviewer suggested; §9 of the task already ties the NaN case to PR10.
- **Doc 215:** status line set to `Completed (C round 288 PASS)`, which stays a claim until C passes. It also gained the two new problem/solution entries, the new test rows and the A-R287-ARCH-ADAPTER-ZERO TODO.
- `VersionSelector.tsx` is untouched; its sha256 equals the round-287 snapshot.

**Results:**
- **Typecheck and lint:** both rc 0. The only warnings in the owned files are older ones at `store.tsx` lines 227–323.
- **Tests:** the 8 covering files pass, 136 tests. `store-focus-ring` and `store-theme-tokens` pass 48/48.
- **Mutants:** N7 fails SC1, N8 fails PC1, N9 and N10 fail PR10 and VC5. N1–N6 were re-run and also go red. The files were restored after each one and their sha256 values checked.
- **Browser smoke at 1440 only:**
  - The label's computed line height is 32 px on `/store` and 28 px on home.
  - Every card measures 589.6 px on `/store` and 417.6 px on home.
  - On `bad-premium-track`, the cards read Standard $19 and Premium "Price unavailable". After selecting Premium, the panel also reads "Price unavailable" and both purchase buttons are `aria-disabled`. There is no `$-5` or `NaN` anywhere on the page.
- **code-reviewer:** 8.5/10, no Critical, High or Medium findings. I added the NaN check it asked for. I kept the PC2 check exactly as B wrote it and noted a tighter version as a proposal for B.

**Notes for C and B:**
- **Fixture description:** my first `bad-premium-track` description wrapped to two lines and made its `/store` row 609.6 px tall. That came from the text, not this change; with a one-line description every card measured 589.6. C should keep that description to one line or the B-LINE-BOX height row can fail for an unrelated reason.
- **Mock readiness:** `curl /api/products/bad-premium-track` returns "Not found" even when the mock serves the product. Use `/api/products` or the product page to check the mock is up.
- **Mock state:** no mock was running on :5199 when I started. I left the standard mock running at the end, with 8 products.
- **Architecture signal for B (not acted on):** the "Price unavailable" label now exists in three places with hand-matched line heights. A shared label component is proposed once `VersionSelector` is unfrozen. Also worth checking: `productAdapter.ts` uses `premiumPrice` without validation, the same family as A-R287-ARCH-ADAPTER-ZERO.

**Not run by me:** 1280×720, comparisons against the `096fa4b` build, the 10-fixture journey and the auth checks. Those are C's rows, and none of B's acceptance rows are claimed. The owned-Standard upgrade view in the browser is blocked because the backend is unavailable in the cloud. The full suite and `verify` are left to the gate.
